questions.q: Why does greedy decoding tend to produce repetitive text?
options: It introduces random noise into the logits before choosing
It always picks the single highest-scoring token and never considers a close second-best, so it has no mechanism to avoid repeating locally-optimal choices
It only samples from the bottom half of the probability distribution
It ignores the model's logits entirely and picks randomly
questions.explain: Greedy decoding (torch.argmax over the logits) is fully deterministic and always takes the top choice, which can lock the model into repetitive loops since it never explores a nearby alternative.

questions.q: What effect does a temperature greater than 1 have on the next-token distribution?
options: It sharpens the distribution, making the output closer to greedy
It has no effect on the distribution shape
It flattens the distribution, giving lower-probability tokens a better chance and increasing output diversity
It removes all but the single highest-probability token
questions.explain: Dividing logits by a temperature greater than 1 before softmax flattens the resulting probability distribution, making lower-probability tokens more likely to be sampled and increasing diversity (at some cost to coherence).

questions.q: In the top-k sampling code, what does torch.multinomial(probs, num_samples=1) do?
options: It deterministically returns the index of the highest value in probs
It draws one random index according to the probability weights in probs — the actual source of randomness in sampling
It sorts probs in descending order
It computes the softmax of probs
questions.explain: torch.multinomial samples indices according to the given probability weights, which is what introduces randomness into top-k (and top-p) sampling, unlike argmax's deterministic choice.

questions.q: How does top-p (nucleus) sampling differ from top-k sampling?
options: Top-p always keeps exactly the same number of candidate tokens as top-k

Top-p keeps a variable-size set of tokens — the smallest group whose cumulative probability exceeds p — so the candidate pool adapts to how confident the model is at each step, unlike top-k's fixed count
Top-p is a deterministic strategy with no sampling involved
Top-p only works with greedy decoding, not with sampling
questions.explain: Top-k always keeps a fixed k candidates, while top-p keeps however many tokens are needed for their cumulative probability to cross p, letting the nucleus shrink when the model is confident and grow when it's uncertain.

questions.q: Which scenario is the best fit for greedy decoding rather than top-k or top-p sampling?
options: Generating creative, varied story continuations
Producing reproducible, deterministic output for debugging or evaluation, where the same input should always yield the same output
Maximizing the diversity of generated vocabulary
Avoiding ever picking the model's single most likely token
questions.explain: Greedy decoding's determinism — same model and prompt always produce the same output — makes it well suited to debugging and reproducible evaluation, even though it sacrifices diversity compared to sampling-based strategies.
